results.title: Okay
results.text:
You may want to engage a guide to fully understand the significance of this venue. 
The entrance fee is relatively high.

results.title: Peace in a chaotic temple
results.text:
The temple itself is very nice - and quite well organized now. However, be careful of unscrupulous priests who can tie a red thread or 'gift' you a rudraksh mala and extort money.

The main sanctum houses a beautiful five faced shiv ling. Must see - from all sides. 

The ancient architecture is also something to admire. Try visiting on a weekday / non-festival / early morning - you may get your peace and quite.

results.title: Amazing temple complex
results.text: I and my wife visited the temple during our recent Nepal tour. The place is beautiful and the complex sprawling. But the cleanliness is poor. There are a lot of touts and scams by the priests. Also the cremation at the river behind the temple is quite nauseating.

Hindu people worshiping there. This place has more then hundreds

results.title: See,Feel and Think
results.text:
This place more then different then other attraction of Kathmandu.
This place totally holy place of Hindu people. The structure of 
temple with different varieties of Gods. This is holy place where Cremation 
will be done after the death of Hindu people just behind this temple on the

results.title: Wonderful experience.
results.text: Visited this place twice,once at the afternoon and another during evening.You can go in without paying the fee (1000nrps for foreigners) after 6.45pm. They usually have this light ceremony with three local priests that pray to god Shiva around 7pm. Pretty interesting ceremony. You can get some flowers (for 'throwing away' your bad habits into the Bagmati river) and sweets(banana, with the blessing from god Shiva) from the priests after the ceremony ends. During the ceremony, you can dance along with the music.

results.title: A must visit place
results.text:
Mobiles and camera are not allowed inside the temple..its said ringing mobiles so you can very well make it silent and take it in..This temple is the main reason lots of people go to kathmandu..you will find lots of decorations in silver on the temples..try to visit the temple with time in hand there is a lot of things that you will see..
Only hindus can enter the temple..

results.title: HOLY PLACE
results.text: The pilgrimage centre of  Kathmandu. The hindu devotees visit here in large number. A large area of temple, relatively clean & holy atmosphere, lots of Sadhus around and pigeons also. When we visited a noble activity of blood donation was going on in the premises.

results.title: Shiv Temple
results.text:
Its like any other Hindu temple. Very crowded , surrounded by touts , pandas asking you to perform Pooja. , not in the temple but in the open garden. Pilgrims are fooled.
Darshan is not so good experience.

results.title: Waste of time
results.text:
It is just a horrible experience going there. 
A commercial temple, selling Hindu beliefs to tourists. 
The so-called sadhus (monks) there, collect money from people to pose for pictures. We had cameras and were approached by these sadhu's agents with opportunities to take pictures at good price !! So much for simple living. 

We couldn't get out of there faster!

results.title: Fascinating cultural experience
results.text: Most westerners definitely have a different idea of how death is dealt with. It may come as a shock to some that the cremation is so public, and the rituals alien to what we're accustomed to, but I found the process as explained by our guide fascinating. Also good photo ops with the Sadhu's and a person dressed as Hanoman. All we could see of the temple complex was from the other side of the river. This was a good start of our tour.

results.title: OK, but not great, and the ongoing cremations are a turnoff
results.text: This is a large Hindu temple complex and perhaps  the best in Kathmandu. That said, there are many more interesting ones in India, so if you are going to India, I am not sure Pashupatinath is worth much time.  Tour guides urge that people see the ongoing cremations there.  Frankly, I've seen it before, and it was both a bit grisly and seemed intrusive to stand and watch families as they conducted these intensely personal ceremonies.  I wouldn't visit again.

results.title: horrible!
results.text: Well, I knew it was a Unesco world heritage site but i didnt know it is gonna be so expensive! 10$ for Nepal....is kinda pricey. Anyway, while bying tickets someguy (obviously a gide) somehow managed to "let me tell you smth about this temple" thing so I was enchanted to listen to his explanation of some Buddhist...things...for good 15 mins! And I didnt want to listen to it at all! And I realised I would have to pay if I dont kick him off me now. So I said i ont wanna listen to him and gave him 250 R (all I had at that time). Temple is terrible, dirty, full of monkeys, cows, their poop, dirty people asking you to buy useless stuff....And u cannot enter the main temple if u r not Hindu. So what's the point of paying so much money? To see the dirt and poop? I saw it enough in Thamel. Anyways, NOT recomended!

results.title: A holy shrine for Hindus dedicated to lord Shiva
results.text:
Pashupatinath temple is one of the holy shrines and highly revered by Hindus. It is a temple of lord Shiva and it was built in 400 AD is almost 1600 years old now.
We visited the temple on June 14th, 2014. It was a good experience and there was not too much rush. We managed to do the Darshan in less than 10 minutes, which otherwise can stretch to 3-4 hours in certain times of the year.
There are hundreds of monkeys in the premises, but they are quite docile and don't attack humans. But they are quite naughty and one of them ran away with my wife's sandals and shred it to bits!

results.title: Its a UNESCO World Heritage Sites!
results.text:
I am not going to share the history and hows beautiful is the temple. :) But i have some tips to share after my Visit.

1. Firstly, please prepare 1000 Nepal Rupee Entrance Fees. this apply to all the foreigner (excluded visitor from Nepal Neighbour country). 

2. Some local guide will be waiting nearby the ticket counter and approach for touring services. Try to talk to them for few minute to make sure they really can speak good english/chinese. Some of them might only good in greeting and introduction. For the touring services, they will ask for 5 USD or 500 Rupee. 

3. a facemask is a MUST. This temple also an Cremation Site. And they did it in open air. 

4. The  Mother Theresa's old folk's home is near beside the temple. Based on my tour guide, this old folk's home have more then 150 old ppl. If you don't mind, just drop some giving to the donation box. :)

As a conclusion, this is a MUST VISIT place. Please don't miss it.

results.title: Om Namath Shivaya
results.text: What a feel amazingly Devine and serene place want to visit many more times. The four side darshana make it unique. There are thousands of shivlings placed in certain order which one touches with both hands and it gives a good feel.

results.title: A must visit when in Kathmandu
results.text: A big temple complex this, cameras and phones not allowed inside the complex though I saw people using them inside. You can greeted to a huge bull idol as you enter the temple and you get a sense of templeception since there are many idols of gods within the complex. The crematorium is visible to public and you can watch all the proceedings. Also once outside the temple complex, it's a haven for portrait photographers. A must visit for people who travel to Kathmandu. It's a 10 minute drive from Thamel, and costs 20 npr if you take one of the mini vans from ranipark

results.title: An beautyful Temple
results.text: I was there with my family last month.Its an beautyful temple.People have strong belive n faith on this temple.We had the pleasure to do the Rudravisekh,which i cant never forget.It was a realy great feling.The surrounding is beautyful.Especially the birds who were in a large numbers to get food from devotees.We enjoyed a lot there.Overall a must visit when u will be at Kathmandu

results.title: Completely divine..!!!
results.text: It is the only best place in kathmandu.You just cannot miss Pashupatinath if you're visiting Kathmandu. The temple in itself is a marvel. It is huge in size. Pashupati ji is located in the centre of the temple surrounded by many small temples. The huge nandi bull is awsome.The temple is amazing, it is chaotic with people everywhere. This is a world famous temple. So don't miss it. You will feel happy and blessed.

results.title: Different in a Good Way
results.text: I was amazed that this crematorium was open for the public viewing pleasure. Numerous cremations were in process allowing me to see various stages in the ritual.
